lib.network_set_query_param.note: OPEN, SET_PARSER 01 01, PARSE (network_json_parse), SET_PARAMETER 00 10, QUERY (256 payload bytes), STATUS 08 00 00 01, STATUS, READ 8 = 'FujiNet' 20, STATUS 00 00 00 88; prints [FujiNet ]
lib.network_set_query_param.surprise: in ASCII output mode (10H) a STRING value's line ending is folded along with it: FNJSON::getValue calls processString(strValue + lineEnding) (fn-h89/lib/fnjson/fnjson.cpp:228) and fn_utf8_to_ascii turns LF, CR and TAB into a space (fn-h89/lib/fntext/fn_sanitize.cpp:658-660). The value ends in 20H, which network_json_strip_newlines() does not remove, so the program gets 'FujiNet ' (8 bytes) instead of 'FujiNet'. Numbers keep their LF (fnjson.cpp:267); the HTML parser appends its line ending after processString (fnhtml.cpp:130) and is not affected. fwspec does not mention it.

lib.network_set_line_ending.note: SET_PARAMETER 01 2C, QUERY '/ports/0', STATUS 04 00 00 01, STATUS, READ 4 = '208,'; the comma is not stripped

lib.network_html_parse.note: OPEN 04 00 'N2:HTTP://127.0.0.1:7802/hello.txt', SET_PARSER 02 02, PARSE: the text/plain page parses (gumbo puts it in <body>)

lib.network_html_query.note: QUERY with 256 payload bytes ('body' and 252 NULs), STATUS 36 00 00 01, STATUS, READ 54 = the page's text with each CR LF made LF by the HTML parser, then the LF line ending; STATUS 00 00 00 88. fujinet-lib strips the last LF: 52 characters, two lines
lib.network_html_query.surprise: fwspec says network_html_query's 256-byte send corrupts the selector, and lists the NUL padding as an open question. On this firmware it works: the RS232 handler does keep all 256 bytes (fn-h89/lib/device/rs232/rs232Network.cpp:9), but gumbo-query's parser stops at the first byte that cannot continue a selector and returns what it has, ignoring the rest (fn-h89/components/gumbo-query/Parser.cpp:52-64, 66-104). What does matter is an '@' anywhere in the 256 bytes: FNHTML::resolveQuery splits the selector at the last '@' and asks for an attribute (fn-h89/lib/fnhtml/fnhtml.cpp:108-115). So keep the selector in a cleared buffer.

lib.network_bus_write.note: OPEN 08 00 'N8:SD:/h89lib.txt', WRITE 19 (network_bus_write to 78H, returns 19), CLOSE. Leaves /h89lib.txt (19 bytes) at the top of the run's SD card, which lib.fuji_file_stat looks up

lib.fuji_file_stat.note: MOUNT_HOST 00, OPEN_DIRECTORY 00 + 256 bytes '' (the top of host 0: the path's directory part is empty), READ_DIR_ENTRY 17 80 (12 + strlen('h89lib.txt') + 1) -> 'test/' (flags 01), READ_DIR_ENTRY 17 80 -> 'h89lib.txt' with size 13 00 00 00 = 19 and the date the run made it (e.g. 38 0A 0D = 2026-10-13: year counts from 1970), CLOSE_DIRECTORY. lib.fuji_file_stat.surprise: none on this file, but only because it is at the top of the SD card: fujinet-pc stats <SD>/<name> instead of <SD>/<dir>/<name> (fn-h89/lib/FileSystem/fnFsSD.cpp:306), so fuji_file_stat() of a file in /test/ would report size 0 and a 1969 date (see expect/exfuji.json fuji.read_dir_entry.ext)
